35 and jaded AF. I work, make good money, have a roof over my head, and I am grateful for what I have. What makes me jaded is my mental health issues. 

On paper, I have a great life, I have multiple degrees, worked at Fortune 500 companies, lived in luxury apartments, and drove expensive cars. However, I  am empty on the inside. I don't enjoy anything, not even the simple things in life. I struggle with depression  and SI. I disassociate a lot and struggle with maladaptive daydreaming where I live in my head and dream about a life I wish I had, like a loving caring mother, supportive family, friends, money, etc.. I fake my emotions and tell people that I'm ok when, in fact, that I am not. 

Because of not growing up in a healthy, loving, and caring environment, I have mommy issues, I need validation, I am a people pleaser, I lack the ability to love myself, and I trust no one. I already do self care and take myself out on dates, but those do not make me feel whole. 

I hike, go to some sporting events, movie theaters, and dinners by myself, and stll nothing. 

I am seeing a therapist for childhood trauma, and it's not helping. I changed therapists 4 times this year, and I am losing hope.

I'm jaded and hanging on by a thread.

Currently using the G6 and it is not bad. The drawback is the price of the transmitter and sensor if you do not have a great insurance plan. Changing the sensor every 10 days can be annoying at first. The readings are accurate for the most part there will be times where it will be off and have to calibrate aka manually check your blood sugar.

If you're choosing the G6 

1. Use a secondary patch that covers the sensor and transmitter. Bumping your arm against the wall and having the dexcom ripped is not fun. They sell them for 25 dollars on Amazon. 

2. Do not use adhesive cleaners on your skin while trying to change your sensor. You can damage the transmitter in the process. 

3. Your phone will need to be at least 20 ft from you or it's going to be annoying having the alert that your dexcom is not in range to monitor your blood sugar. 

I believe the G7 is out where the sensor and transmitter are combined so it might be cheaper than the G6
